title: Wayfare Pass Frequent-Rider Correction Relief — Questions Answered
content:
# Frequent-rider correction relief — Wayfare Pass (rider membership)

**What is the frequent-rider correction relief?**
When Pass ride credit is clawed back from a Wayfare Pass member because a fare was reduced by a fare adjustment, the frequent-rider correction relief counts the member's trips charged a fare in the last three months: 15 percent at 20 or more, 5 percent at 10 to 19, nothing below 10.

**What is counted?**
Fare charges on the member's trips in Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares), dated in the last three months, one per trip charged a fare.

**How does it act?**
The relief takes that percentage of the clawed-back credit on the trip off the credit correction. The percentage is of the clawed-back credit itself; the credit correction never goes below 0.00, and it is rounded half up to the cent once the relief is taken off.

**Where are the edges?**

| Trips charged a fare in the last three months | Relief |
|---|---|
| 20 or more | 15 percent |
| 10 to 19 | 5 percent |
| 0 to 9 | nothing |

20 trips give 15 percent and 19 give 5 percent; 10 trips give 5 percent and 9 give nothing.

**A figure?** (hypothetical) With 1.80 clawed back and 22 fare charges in the last three months, 0.27 is taken off, leaving 1.53.
